I think these constants should be `static constexpr` members of `SingleFab`, as they are only supposed to be used by `SingleFab`.
"or will create PEL in case of invalid scenario" ?

`return (i_imValue.substr(0, 4) == POWER10_IM_SERIES) ? true : false;`
We do not need ternary operator here.

`return (i_imValue.substr(0, 4) == POWER10_IM_SERIES)` serves the purpose.

`return (i_imValue.substr(0, 4) == POWER11_IM_SERIES) ? true : false;`
We do not need ternary operator here.

`return (i_imValue.substr(0, 4) == POWER11_IM_SERIES)` serves the purpose.

As we already have two methods `isP10System()` and `isP11System()`, this implementation can be simplified to: 

`return isP10System(l_imValue) || isP11System(l_imValue);`

Move this code out of try/catch block and use the return code from "singleFabImOverride" to mark the situation where BMC needs to be quiesced. Then throw from here so that main catches the exception and mark the service as failed?

Do you see any downside in case we do this?
@sunnsr25@in.ibm.com, One downside I see of moving `singleFabImOverride()` out of `try` `catch` block is if `singleFabImOverride()` API throws exception due to any STL call or other method failure.

> Move this code out of try/catch block and use the return code from "singleFabImOverride" to mark the situation where BMC needs to be quiesced.


That is why I said to have return codes instead of throw from the singleFab API.
Rest of the exception can be handled locally and specific return code can be sent back to mark situation where BMC should be quiesced. 
Based on that we can throw from here and fail the service.
Return int from this API and have some specific error code defined so that its return code can be used to set BMC to Quiesced state?

Do we need string copy or reference can be used as it is already const?
Same for others.
In case it is not being used in hpp file itself, its better to have these definitions local to cpp file.
Defined this under vpd namespace. so this can be used in manager.cpp file to check for invalid case.

I think its better to define an enum for the possible return codes of `SingleFabImOverride` API. For eg. `enum class SingleFabReturnVal { INVALID_CASE=-2, FAILURE=-1,SUCCESS=0};`

Having a `INVALID_CASE` variable does not make it immediately clear what and where it is being used for.
no need for invalid case. failure is an invalid case and is handled
